source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10. Step 1, exact partial doubling of the table's own CA(33;3,121,2) (Power CT over GF(11), row S7): 34 of its columns are written a second time and 8 helper rows are added, a strength-2 family on 8 rows with each twinned column and its twin complementary, giving CA(41;3,155,2) (programs/pd155.py; valid because 34 + 1 <= C(7,4)). Step 2, the 33 rows of the 121 base columns are kept fixed and everything else may change (the 8 helper rows, the 34 twin columns and 8 new columns); simulated annealing with exact counts on the triples that contain a column beyond the base starts from the array of step 1 with 8 random columns added (programs/pad.py PD_41_3_155_2.txt 41 163 5 start.txt, then programs/ext3.c, command ext3 CA_33_3_121_2.txt 33 121 8 42 32 300 1.0 out -i start.txt, 0 uncovered at 124 s). Exact check with ca_verify, all 3-sets
construction: Partial Roux doubling of the Power CT CA(33;3,121,2) (34 columns doubled, 8 helper rows, 155 columns), then 8 columns added by annealing with the base fixed
notes: ties the cited size 41 at k = 163; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
